answer: Each identity forges its standing like an opal — but the opal only shows its true colors when seen from many angles: each piece of work must be verified by distinct, established identities who are not connected to each other, so no single cluster of friends can vouch for it. A wander of trust grows only from verifications that come from different corners of the network, and a fake that is only seen from one angle stays dull: each fake must earn fresh, independent witnesses, one angle at a time, and witnesses who share a cluster do not count twice.
